question: Should OpenClaw consolidate memory behavior through the open role-slot/API work, a simpler `memory.type` product surface, or a docs/doctor-only clarification of the existing builtin/QMD/plugin model?
rationale: Current main still has multiple memory mechanisms and the requested fix changes durable public config, plugin API, storage, docs, and migration behavior that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Review role-slot PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as the main implementation review path, then keep this issue focused on any remaining memory UX/storage consistency gaps.

options.title: Narrow to docs and doctor UX
options.body: Avoid new memory API/config surface for now and make existing builtin, QMD, plugin-slot, and Markdown behaviors easier to diagnose and migrate.

options.title: Reject core reshaping
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide current plugin/backend seams are sufficient and memory composition should remain external or plugin-owned.

recommendation.title: Review role-slot PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as the main implementation review path, then keep this issue focused on any remaining memory UX/storage consistency gaps.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is product/API direction across public config, plugin contracts, and memory UX, and steipete is the strongest decision-owner signal from repository docs and history.
